title: A device that turns reminders on settles its own row after a later erase
evidence: Built to the owner's option A (2026-11-25). The page that writes a reminders token keeps { token, erase } in one localStorage key (hr_reminders_own_enrolment) as one state, OwnEnrolment (none | kept | cancelling), changed only by the pure ownEnrolmentTransition (widget-src/standalone/reminders-own-enrolment.ts), following the record's owed-clear pattern (clearOwed / settleClear, packages/health-core/src/record-session.ts). It settles at load and on every hr:remote-changed: a record at a later erase (eraseLater) that does not hold the token active gets one keepalive cancel. The key stays until a cancel answers 2xx (owner ruling Q1, amending US-11 AC4): a failed one retries at the next load and the next merged-in change. A claim stored before the post keeps a second tab silent; one older than CLAIM_MS (a minute) is taken again. Nothing settles while this tab's erase runs; this device's Turn off and its own erase commit (when it cancels the token) remove the key. Wiring: reminders.ts optInToReminders (enrolled) and cancelReminders (turned-off), reminders-erase-cancel.ts stepEraseCancel on committed (erased-here), standalone/app.tsx startOwnEnrolment. No merge, health-core or iOS change. Tests: widget-src/standalone/reminders-own-enrolment.test.ts (8 behaviour tests over the real store and an in-memory cloud, each failing first or shown against a named mutation, and the 19-row transition table). The erasing page's running-save pin in reminders-erase-cancel.test.ts stays as it is: that page still does not cancel another device's token; the enrolling page does. US-11 AC4 and AC4c amended. Residual: a device that enrolled and never opens the page again keeps its row until the email unsubscribe link is used.
